decisive_items: Six months earlier he had resumed antiretroviral therapy, with his CD4 count rising from 94 to 160 cells/mm3; the lip lesions developed approximately two months after the CD4 count began to improve.
He had received multiple courses of antibiotics and systemic corticosteroids without benefit.
Diagnostic studies showed an undetectable HIV viral load and undetectable hepatitis C viral load.
response.rationale: The temporal association of symptom onset with immune reconstitution, lack of response to antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory therapy, and negative workup for common infectious and non-infectious causes strongly support IRIS.

rejected.why: Negative fungal cultures, Histoplasma antigen, and mucicarmine stain rule out fungal infection.
Normal C1 esterase inhibitor and presence of ulcerations are inconsistent with angioedema.
Negative HSV PCR and ongoing acyclovir prophylaxis make HSV unlikely.
Lack of response to multiple courses of antibiotics and absence of typical vascular lesions make this unlikely.
